etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English continuel, from Old French continuel, formed from Latin continuus (“continuous”) with the suffix -el, equivalent to continue +‎ -al.

quote.citation: 2022 January 12, Paul Bigland, “Fab Four: the nation's finest stations: Wakefield Kirkgate”, in RAIL, number 948, page 28:
quote.text: The history of this station is one of continual rebuilding.

definitions.definition: (proscribed) Seemingly continuous; appearing to have no end or interruption.
